co_redgarden_tower_two.blurb: Tower Two is the tallest, most sought-after section of Eldorado Canyon's biggest wall: a red sandstone buttress of slabs, chimneys, ramps, roofs and a big headwall above. Nearly all of the climbing is traditional and much of it is multi-pitch, with a handful of bolted lines mixed in. The grades pile up in the 5.11 range, with a decent spread of 5.9 to 5.10 and a few 5.13s. Classics include The Naked Edge, Rosy Crucifixion, T2 and The Diving Board. Some lines are bold and sparsely protected, and fixed gear is old. Work out your descent before leaving the ground, since the walk-offs and rappels are long, and carry shoes and a layer for the trip down.
co_redgarden_tower_two.parking_note: Park inside the state park near the east end of the canyon road. From there a short uphill walk leads to the footbridge over the creek, and trails fork toward the base of the buttress.

co_east_quarry_the.blurb: The East Quarry is a newer, harder corner of North Table Mountain, cut into dark volcanic basalt above Golden. It is mostly bolted face and corner climbing, with a fair amount of trad as well, and the sport lines lean steep: most of the grades sit in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few 5.13s and only a handful of easy leads. Slap Happy, Flying Fish, Wooly Bully and Chum are among the best-known lines. The stone gets polished and can feel greasy on warm days, rattlesnakes are around in summer and fall, and anchors are worn, so rappel or lower with care. It is a good cool-weather choice.
co_east_quarry_the.parking_note: Use the lots off Easley Road reached from the MacIntyre exit of CO 58, on the east side of the mesa. This is separate from the lots serving the main Golden Cliffs.

co_little_eiger.blurb: Little Eiger is a roadside crag in Clear Creek Canyon, west of Golden, with tall, nearly vertical gneiss that is unusual for the canyon. Most of the climbing is bolted sport, mainly 5.10 and 5.11, with a few moderates, some 5.12s and a scattering of boulder problems near the base. Eiger Direct, Busch Gardens and Too! are among the best-known lines. The walls are tall, so bring a long rope and tie a knot in the end. Across the road, the shaded canyon wall forms short ice and mixed climbs in cold winters, among them Maharaja. Parking is cramped, so stay in the marked pullouts.
co_little_eiger.parking_note: Use the roadside pullouts on US 6 near the first bridge above the lower tunnel, roughly three and a half miles into the canyon. Space is limited; stay in the marked spots.

co_turkey_rock.blurb: Turkey Rock is the main formation at Turkey Rocks in the South Platte, a coarse granite buttress known for crack climbing, with scattered face moves on its sunny south side. Climbs reach about three pitches and are almost all traditional, with most grades from 5.8 to 5.10 and some 5.11s above that. Gobbler's Grunt, Straw Turkey, Vanishing Point and Turkey Shoot are among the favorites. The granite is rough on skin, so tape is worth bringing, and a full rack with extra mid-size cams helps. Shade is limited on the south face, which makes summer afternoons hot, so start early or wait for cooler weather. Walk-offs are straightforward.
co_turkey_rock.parking_note: Reach the area on the Forest Service dirt road to the Turkey Rocks trailhead and campground, which can be rutted. The neighboring subdivision has no public parking, so use the trailhead.

co_corona_crag.blurb: Corona Crag is the main bouldering zone in Mitchell Creek Canyon, a small canyon near Castle Rock cut in pebbly conglomerate. The problems are bunched within a short stretch of hillside and cover slab, vertical and overhanging styles, on holds that are mostly solid, with flakes, jugs and crimps. Most of the established problems are in the V0 to V4 range, which makes it friendly for newer boulderers, though there are also several V7 to V10 lines and a few harder ones. Safety First, Mobile Morgue and The Crypt are well known. Rattlesnakes have been seen near the trails, so watch your step in warm months, and bring pads.
co_corona_crag.parking_note: Park at the Gateway Mesa open space lot and walk the canyon trail.

co_widowmakers.blurb: Widowmakers is a bouldering area in the Narrows of Poudre Canyon, a steep talus field beneath the Electric Ocean Wall. Problems run from V0 up to double-digit V grades with a good spread through the middle grades, and the stone is a touch rough in places with some uneven landings, so pads and a spotter help. Most boulders are only minutes from the car, while a few are a longer scramble up the slope. Jungle Juice and Le Don are the standouts. Many climbers treat it as the backup to the better-quality Narrows boulders a few minutes further up the canyon.

co_north_east_boulders.blurb: The North-East Boulders are a cluster of granite blocks beside the road north of Empire, at about 8,600 feet. Adhesion is good, and the typical problem is short and steep with open-hand moves and a power-oriented sequence of about six moves to the top, mostly V3 to V6, with a good number of V6 to V8 lines too and a couple of harder tests. Road Warrior, Crowd Chaser and Empire Fridge are among the best known. Landings are mostly flat but rocky, so bring pads. The boulders sit under a minute from the road, which makes for a quick session, and more rocks lie across the road and upstream. The season can run longer into fall than the elevation suggests.
co_north_east_boulders.parking_note: Roadside pullouts about 3.2 miles north of the stoplight by the Empire post office, on the highway toward Berthoud Pass. Use the second of the two big pullouts.
co_north_east_boulders.approach: A trail beside a small granite face on the north side of the road, marked by a large cairn, reaches the first boulders in under a minute.

_expect.name: West Ridge - part A - Verschneidung to base

co_west_ridge_part_a_verschneidung_to_ba.blurb: This is the lower end of the West Ridge in Eldorado Canyon, running from the foot of the ridge up to the Verschneidung dihedral, on red sandstone that faces southwest. Almost all of it is trad, and the grades cluster around 5.9, with a second group in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. It is the quieter side of the canyon, with shorter lines than the big walls. Verschneidung Dihedral, Allosaur, Morning Thunder and Wild Turkey are the best-known lines. The base is sunny through the afternoon, and the approach depends on creek level: wade or boulder-hop near the east end, or follow the creek trail and cross a slippery ramp. Rappel or scramble down the back of the ridge.
co_west_ridge_part_a_verschneidung_to_ba.parking_note: Either park at the east end of the state park and follow the creek trail from the bridge, or use the small Milton Boulder pullout where the creek is crossed on foot. The pullout holds few cars.
